template_name: Housing needs plan or housing element
description: A plan for housing: who needs what, what stands in the way, where capacity exists, and the programs the agency commits to.
scope_notes: This is a standard-practice starting point — edit to your scope. Rename, delete and add records until the list matches the work your agency actually agreed to do.

Every date is calculated forward from the kickoff date you enter. The offsets are round numbers reflecting how this kind of work is usually sequenced — they are placeholders for a real schedule, not commitments.

Housing plans are among the most heavily regulated planning documents there are, and the required contents, review steps, outside approvals and deadlines differ by state and country. Nothing here states a requirement — confirm what your jurisdiction asks for and add the records it needs, including any review by an outside agency before adoption.
The site inventory is the deliverable most often challenged after adoption. Record the evidence for each site's capacity as you go, not afterwards.

No jurisdiction is assumed. Review periods, required notices, hearings and the body that adopts the work are set where you are; none of them are stated here. Add the records your own process requires.
Nobody is assigned. Applying a template never puts a colleague's name on a deadline — assign the records yourself once the team is settled.

deliverables.title: Housing needs assessment
deliverables.summary: Households, incomes, cost burden, overcrowding, homelessness and special housing needs, with sources named.

deliverables.title: Constraints analysis
deliverables.summary: The governmental and non-governmental barriers to producing housing, described concretely rather than generally.

deliverables.title: Site inventory and capacity analysis
deliverables.summary: The sites relied on for capacity, each with the evidence that it can realistically develop.

deliverables.title: Housing access and equity assessment
deliverables.summary: Patterns of segregation, displacement risk and access to opportunity, and the actions proposed in response.

deliverables.title: Draft goals, policies and housing programs
deliverables.summary: The commitments the agency proposes to make, each with a responsible party and a timeframe.

deliverables.title: Public review draft
deliverables.summary: The complete draft released for public review.

deliverables.title: Final housing element or plan
deliverables.summary: The draft revised after public and any outside-agency review.

milestones.title: Project kickoff meeting
milestones.summary: Scope, schedule and the engagement approach confirmed.

milestones.title: Community meetings on housing need
milestones.summary: Renters, owners, service providers and people who have been priced out are heard early.

milestones.title: Builder and service provider roundtable
milestones.summary: The people who produce and operate housing test the draft programs for realism.

milestones.title: Public review of the draft opens
milestones.summary: The draft is released for comment.

milestones.title: Adoption of the housing element or plan
